refutations.why_it_matters: Not stale documentation: 181 September misses post-date the 09-11 receipt, so the number is actively worsening. git shows no committed deletion, so these are uncommitted bytes that vanished or were never written, while the append-only chain names them as existing.
refutations.falsifier: A post-2026-09-11 restore receipt re-creating the 1199 August filenames as bytes, or proof the 1380 resolve to a second store (cage copy / .mimosa snapshot) — the latter would make this a naming bug, not a loss bug.

refutations.claim: 'Hook wiring is correct. core.hooksPath = githooks, githooks/pre-push present and executable (17,853 bytes). No stray .git/hooks/pre-push.' — listed under 'What is healthy'
refutations.why_it_matters: All three factual sub-claims are true; the health conclusion they support is not. 5 of 8 push-gate blocks are self-declared NEVER-exit-nonzero with TODO-FLIP-TO-ENFORCE comments. The census drift that IS real does not block a push. 'Hook exists' and 'hook enforces the estate's laws' are incomparable claims; the prior map reported the first and let it stand for the second.

The sidecar is real and byte-accurate, but it is a FLAT LOOKUP TABLE with no parent link, so it cannot be part of any hash chain. 'Reconciled' describes a join, not a reconciliation. 13,687 is a hand-typed markdown number 9 off from the only real count — the 1341 fossil in new costume. The script's own docstring is honest ('INDEX-ONLY row', 'sidecar is merge-later'); the prose layered on top was not.

findings.title: baseline-update is an ungated, zero-exit, self-widening write that defaults its own author to "operator"
findings.why_it_matters: The machine can widen its own gate in one command whose only input is the debt it just found. The docstring's law 'can only grow by a human/agent running baseline-update, never silently' is not enforced by anything. The gopher F4 framing 'accept by NAME ... No silent baseline widening' is refuted: naming it and absorbing it silently are the SAME command.

THIS IS THE INHERITED BLINDNESS: detection runs on ast.parse against a hardcoded SCANNER_RULES set of 9. Any disease outside those 9 is invisible by construction. 652 except-pass claims prove the rule fires; nothing proves the rule SET is the right 9.

structurally_absent_questions.question: If every instrument in this estate was built inside the hall of mirrors, what experiment could distinguish 'the estate is healthy' from 'the estate's instruments consistently agree with each other because they all share the same blind spot'?
structurally_absent_questions.archive_evidence: extracted 1414 question sentences from 1447 markdown files under watch/inbox/; tested 16 interrogative themes; zero hits on cross-instrument disagreement / 'would your instruments even notice'
structurally_absent_questions.why_structurally_absent: Every meter derives from the same os.walk + json.loads + same tree. The estate has N instruments and 1 viewpoint. A second opinion does not exist, so it cannot appear as a gap in a list of gaps.

structurally_absent_questions.question: Which numbers we are about to publish would still be true if the estate's definitions changed tomorrow — and who is allowed to change a definition without invalidating the number?
structurally_absent_questions.archive_evidence: the archive asks about drift of VALUES (the 12-to-1380 case) and never about drift of UNITS. 'disk 349 vs carrier 303' was dismissed as instrument lag when it is a units dispute; 13687 is a units dispute (prose vs sidecar rows).
structurally_absent_questions.why_structurally_absent: B2-249 makes the census number depend on the exact English grammar of the AGENTS.md:27 bullet — rewording the sentence breaks the gate. The most-cited number in the estate is hostage to markdown wording, and no question in the archive notices.

structurally_absent_questions.question: If the only remedy the enforcement point offers is 'run this other command', and that command always exits 0 and defaults its own author to "operator", is the enforcement point an enforcement point?
structurally_absent_questions.archive_evidence: SOCRATIC_GAPS_20260918.md asks 'who audits the auditor's corrections?' — 2 hits, both rhetorical, never answered. Zero hits on a machine widening its own gate, outside this document.
structurally_absent_questions.why_structurally_absent: The archive's framing is 'who audits' (an identity question). The sharper structural form is 'is the audit trail's own write path the thing being audited' — a mechanism question, which is a different kind of object and so never gets asked.

structurally_absent_questions.question: What is the estate's rate of un-receipted reality — bytes that changed with no card, no queue row, and no chain knot — and is that number measured at all?
structurally_absent_questions.archive_evidence: every instrument counts ARTIFACTS (cards, knots, claims, files). Not one counts SILENCE. 1380 vanished knots produced no receipt; 1379 untracked paths produced no drift alarm; the census carrier moved 1910->2294 with no card.
structurally_absent_questions.why_structurally_absent: Absence of a receipt is treated as absence of an event. A meter that can only see what was written down is structurally incapable of noticing what wasn't — so unrecorded change can never surface as a gap, even though it is the class of thing that has actually happened.

structurally_absent_questions.question: Whose decision is it to retire a number — and is that decision ever recorded anywhere?
structurally_absent_questions.archive_evidence: state/CURRENT.md frozen 09-08 and still cited as live status; the census carrier was hand-edited within one minute of its own detector firing; configs/violation_baseline.json holds 933 claims with 0 expiries.
structurally_absent_questions.why_structurally_absent: The estate has no expiry on its own claims and no named owner for retiring one. The 933-claim immortal baseline and the hand-edited carrier are the same disease, and no document in the archive connects them.

question_archive_method.caveat: regex sentence extraction over markdown; counts are indicative of theme presence/absence, not a semantic census. The four absent themes are corroborated by the positive controls (sibling themes DID match, e.g. 'who holds the knife', 'searchable by whom?', 'decision-decay').

top_recommendation: Do not build this audit on the prior map. Re-derive from bytes. The three findings that survive every tool-substitution available to me are: 1380 missing knots, the ratchet seeing 39% of tracked Python, and baseline-update being an ungated self-widening zero-exit write that forges by="operator". All three use no fleet instrument.
